fullPassage:
Consumer Activism

Consumer activism involves consumers taking actions to support or protest certain products or companies based on their ethical, environmental, or social concerns. A boycott is a form of protest in which individuals stop purchasing products from a particular company to express their objection to its practices. For example, in 2010, Greenpeace, an environmental support organization, initiated a campaign against a product of a food company, accusing the company of sourcing palm oil from companies involved in the destruction of forests. In response to Greenpeace's campaign and growing public pressure, the company agreed to cease sourcing palm oil from companies linked with the destruction of forests and commit to using sustainable palm oil by 2015.

Today, a new form of consumer activism, known as a buycott, has emerged. In a buycott, consumers actively support companies in accord with their values by consciously buying their products. In 2020, an ice cream brand gained attention for its support of climate action. Consumers who shared this value actively purchased the ice cream, enhancing its reputation and sales. This inspired other brands to consider their social and environmental responsibilities.

In this way, consumer activism empowers individuals to use their purchasing power and voices to promote positive change and hold businesses accountable for their actions.
